subtitle: On the Dust Road to Chenna Mallikarjuna

panels.shot: wide, low-angle view of a lone woman on a dusty Deccan road, village fading behind, distant hills ahead
panels.action: Akka Mahadevi walks barefoot along a sunlit track, simple white cloth around her, hair loose, eyes fixed on distant blue hills of the Deccan, as fields and a village recede into haze behind her.

dialogue.text: In twelfth-century Karnataka, Akka Mahadevi left home for the open road, turning bare Kannada words into a revolt of love for Chenna Mallikarjuna.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी का कर्नाटक। अक्का घर छोड़कर निकल पड़ी, नंगे कन्नड़ शब्दों को चेन्‍ना मल्लिकार्जुन के लिए प्रेम के बग़ावत में बदलते हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot, interior of a modest village house, warm lamp light on a young girl by the doorway
panels.action: Young Akka Mahadevi stands at a doorway in Udutadi, clutching a palm-leaf manuscript, glancing from the script to the temple gopura outside as oil lamps flicker.

dialogue.text: The legends give her many births, but the vachanas give us a voice: a village girl from Udutadi, turning towards a god she calls Chenna Mallikarjuna.

i18n.hi: कथाएँ उसे कई जन्म देती हैं, पर वचन हमें एक आवाज़ देते हैं: उदुतडी की गाँव की लड़की, उस देव की ओर मुड़ती जिसे वो चेन्‍ना मल्लिकार्जुन कहती है।

panels.shot: close-up on Akka Mahadevi’s face, half lit by lamp, lips just parting as if speaking
panels.action: Akka Mahadevi sits cross-legged in a dim room, palm-leaf in her lap, eyes closed in concentration as her lips form silent words to an unseen presence.

dialogue.text: In her own lines she is not a queen or a sage in a court. She is a woman who has already chosen a husband in her heart.

i18n.hi: अपनी पंक्तियों में वो न रानी है, न दरबार की ऋषि। वो एक औरत है जिसने दिल ही दिल में अपना पति चुन लिया है।

panels.shot: medium shot, village shrine courtyard, Akka before a linga under a tree
panels.action: Akka Mahadevi stands before a simple stone linga under a broad tree, hands folded, while villagers move about in the background, barely noticing her stillness.

dialogue.speaker: akka_mahadevi
dialogue.text: Chenna Mallikarjuna, if I have you, what else do I need?

i18n.hi: चेन्‍ना मल्लिकार्जुन, तुम हो तो मुझे और क्या चाहिए?

panels.shot: wide shot of a bustling temple courtyard, priests, donors, and women in ritual, Akka at the edge observing
panels.action: In a larger town temple courtyard, priests carry trays, drums are silent but poised, and richly dressed women circle the shrine, while Akka Mahadevi stands apart, watching, her face sharp with doubt.

dialogue.text: Around her, temples grow rich on ritual. Her vachanas slice through the smoke, asking if god can be bought with incense and caste.

i18n.hi: उसके चारों तरफ़ मंदिर रस्मों से मालामाल। उसके वचन धुएँ को चीरते हैं, पूछते हैं: क्या भगवान धूप और जात से खरीदे जाते हैं?

panels.shot: medium close-up of Akka, tense, in a richer household space, older figures gesturing towards her
panels.action: Inside a better-off house, elders in fine cloth point towards Akka Mahadevi as if explaining plans, while she looks down at her hands, fingers tightening around her shawl.

dialogue.text: Later storytellers tie her to kings and forced marriage. The poems themselves only show a woman pressed by a world that wants her bound.

i18n.hi: बाद के किस्सागो उसे राजाओं और ज़बरन शादी से बाँधते हैं। खुद कविता बस एक औरत दिखाती है जिसे वो दुनिया धकेल रही है जो उसे बाँधना चाहती है।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Akka’s hands loosening jewelry, resting them on a low wooden chest
panels.action: Akka Mahadevi’s hands delicately remove bangles and a necklace, laying them on a small wooden chest beside folded household cloths.

dialogue.text: Again and again she calls worldly marriage a bargain too small. In one vachana, she says she has no use for men who cannot match her chosen lord.

i18n.hi: बार‑बार वो कहती है, दुनिया की शादी बहुत छोटा सौदा है। एक वचन में कहती है, उन मर्दों से उसे काम नहीं जो उसके चुने स्वामी की बराबरी न कर सकें।

panels.shot: medium shot, threshold of the house at dawn, Akka stepping out, family dim in the background
panels.action: At grey dawn, Akka Mahadevi steps over the worn threshold with a cloth bundle, her family faint in the shadows behind her, one hand half-raised as if to call her back.

dialogue.text: Somewhere between memory and myth, there is a simple act: she leaves. The vachanas remember the leaving, not the names of those she defied.

i18n.hi: याद और मिथक के बीच एक सीधा काम रह जाता है: वो चली जाती है। वचन बस इस जाते हुए को याद रखते हैं, न उन नामों को जिन्हें वो ठुकराती है।

panels.shot: wide shot of the open country road, Akka small but central, sky vast above
panels.action: Akka Mahadevi walks alone along a winding road between rocky fields, goats grazing in the distance, clouds opening to blue above her.

dialogue.text: She takes the open road: from Udutadi towards the new wind in Kalyana, where Basavanna and others are already breaking rank and caste.

i18n.hi: वो खुली सड़क पकड़ती है: उदुतडी से कल्याण की नई हवा की ओर, जहाँ बसवन्ना और दूसरे पहले ही जाती और बिरादरी तोड़ रहे हैं।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Basavakalyana’s Anubhava Mantapa, simple hall filled with seated men and a few women
panels.action: In Basavakalyana, a plain pillared hall is crowded with men and some women seated in a circle, heads bare but for simple cloths, as Akka Mahadevi steps hesitantly into the doorway.

dialogue.text: Lingayat memory calls it the Anubhava Mantapa. Whatever its exact walls, the record is clear: a space where Basavanna and Allama Prabhu welcome a woman’s fierce tongue.

i18n.hi: लिंगायत याद उसे अनुभव मंटप कहती है। दीवारें जैसी भी रही हों, बात साफ़ है: ऐसी जगह जहाँ बसवन्ना और अल्‍लमा प्रभु एक औरत की तीखी ज़ुबान का स्वागत करते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot from behind Akka, facing the assembly, some skeptical, some curious
panels.action: From behind Akka Mahadevi, we see faces of sharanas turned towards her—one old man frowns, another smiles slightly, a younger woman looks on with bright curiosity.

dialogue.text: The Sunyasampadane preserves their debates. It remembers her not as a guest, but as one of them—a speaker whose words can sting even the leaders.

i18n.hi: शून्‍य संपादने में उनके वाद–विवाद बसे हैं। वो उसे मेहमान नहीं, अपने में से एक मानता है—ऐसी वक्ता जिसकी चोट नेताओं तक को लगती है।

panels.shot: close-up on Akka speaking, eyes steady, mouth set, a simple linga on a thread at her neck
panels.action: Akka Mahadevi stands with chin raised, a simple stone linga hanging at her neck, lips parted as she addresses the gathered saints.

dialogue.speaker: akka_mahadevi
dialogue.text: If you call it devotion and still crave status, what is different in you?

i18n.hi: अगर इसे भक्ती कहते हो और फिर भी ओहदा चाहते हो, तो तुममें फर्क क्या रहा?

panels.shot: medium wide shot of the Mantapa, sharanas absorbed, one elder slightly chastened
panels.action: Within the hall, some sharanas lean forward, others look down as if struck, while Akka stands unwavering in the center, hands open.

dialogue.text: Her vachanas insist: a sharana must break caste, leave hollow rituals, strip away every borrowed identity. This, she says, includes the pride of men who preach equality.

i18n.hi: उसके वचन अड़ कर कहते हैं: शरण को जात तोड़नी होगी, खोखली रस्म छोड़नी होगी, हर उधार की पहचान उतारनी होगी। इसमें, वो कहती है, बराबरी का उपदेश देने वाले मर्दों का अहं भी आता है।

panels.shot: close-up on a palm-leaf being inscribed, stylus carving short, sharp lines
panels.action: A hand, perhaps that of a scribe or fellow sharana, carves short, uneven lines into a palm leaf, the strokes swift and spare.

dialogue.text: In this circle, Kannada changes. The vachana, a terse spoken line, becomes scripture of the street. Akka’s name stands among the strongest, with hundreds of verses remembered.

i18n.hi: इस गोले में कन्नड़ बदलता है। बोलचाल का छोटा वचन गली का शास्त्र बन जाता है। अक्का का नाम सबसे तेज़ों में गिना जाता है, सैकड़ों वचन ज़बानी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Akka among common folk on a street, reciting, listeners include a washerman, a woman vendor, a child
panels.action: On a dusty street near the Mantapa, Akka Mahadevi stands beneath a tree, reciting, while a washerman, a vegetable seller woman and a child listen in rapt attention.

dialogue.text: The vachana form carries her beyond halls and royal courts. Her Chenna Mallikarjuna travels in the mouths of washermen, potters, farmers, women who had never owned a Sanskrit word.

i18n.hi: वचन का रास्ता उसे हॉलों और दरबारों से बाहर ले जाता है। उसका चेन्‍ना मल्लिकार्जुन धोबियों, कुम्हारों, किसानों, उन औरतों की ज़बान पर चलता है जिन्होंने कभी संस्कृत छुआ भी नहीं।

panels.shot: medium wide shot, faint outline of Basavakalyana behind, Akka turning away onto another road
panels.action: Outside Basavakalyana, its walls dim in the background, Akka Mahadevi stands at a fork in the path, turning towards a rocky, tree-lined route leading south.

dialogue.text: Hagiographers send her next to Srisailam, tell of miracles and a final vanishing into light. The poems themselves fall silent on her end.

i18n.hi: चरितकार उसे आगे श्रीशैलम भेजते हैं, चमत्कारों और उजाले में लय होने की बात कहते हैं। खुद वचन उसके अंत पर चुप हो जाते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of rugged hills and forested slope, Akka a small figure climbing
panels.action: A tiny figure of Akka Mahadevi climbs a rugged, forested hillside, mist pooling in the valleys, while distant stone shrines dot the ridge.

dialogue.text: Yet the direction fits: she writes of Chenna Mallikarjuna as if the deity lives not in one stone, but in wind, rock, and the quiet between syllables.

i18n.hi: फिर भी दिशा जचती है: वो चेन्‍ना मल्लिकार्जुन को ऐसे लिखती है जैसे देव एक पत्थर में नहीं, हवा, पहाड़ और अक्षरों के बीच की ख़ामोशी में बसता हो।

panels.shot: close-up of Akka seated in meditation near a rocky shrine, eyes half-closed, face calm
panels.action: Akka Mahadevi sits near a small rock shrine, legs folded, spine straight, eyes half-closed, the hint of a smile softening her face.

dialogue.speaker: akka_mahadevi
dialogue.text: When I am with you, Chenna Mallikarjuna, the world’s noise is a distant drum.

i18n.hi: जब मैं तुम्हारे साथ हूँ, चेन्‍ना मल्लिकार्जुन, दुनिया की हलचल बस दूर की ढोलक है।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of a preserved manuscript leaf, Akka’s name and deity-signature visible in old Kannada script
panels.action: An aged palm-leaf manuscript rests on a wooden desk in soft light, the old Kannada letters of Akka Mahadevi’s name and her Chenna Mallikarjuna signature clearly visible.

dialogue.text: Her body’s end is unknown, but her words endured: spare, fearless, a woman’s voice that refused every borrowed cage to walk, forever, on the open road of language.

i18n.hi: उसके शरीर का अंत अनसुना रहा, पर शब्द टिके रहे: सादे, निडर, एक औरत की आवाज़ जिसने हर उधार की कैद ठुकराई और हमेशा के लिए भाषा की खुली सड़क पकड़ ली।

title_i18n.en: Akka Mahadevi Takes the Open Road
title_i18n.hi: अक्का महादेवी का खुली सड़क पर सफ़र

subtitle_i18n.en: On the Dust Road to Chenna Mallikarjuna
subtitle_i18n.hi: धूल भरी सड़क से चेन्‍ना मल्लिकार्जुन की ओर
